en.headline: Electronic advance medical directives to go live on eHealth next year
en.dek: Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun said in a written reply that residents will be able to create, store and revoke directives electronically on the platform in phases, with the same legal effect as paper.
body: Hongkongers will be able to create advance medical directives electronically on the eHealth platform as early as next year, setting out which life-sustaining treatments they do not wish to receive if they become terminally ill, the government said.

In a written reply to lawmakers on Wednesday, Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun Yuk-han said the electronic service, which currently exists only in paper form, would be rolled out in phases after consulting units including the Health Bureau. eHealth will serve as the designated system for residents to make, store and revoke a directive.

Authorities said the digital version will carry the same legal effect as the paper version. Do-not-attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders will remain in hard copy. The Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance, which took effect on 31 July this year, already allows mentally competent adults to make such directives in writing with witnesses, including a registered medical practitioner.

zh.headline: 預設醫療指示明年可在醫健通電子化訂立
zh.dek: 勞工及福利局局長孫玉菡書面回覆指，市民可分階段在平台訂立、儲存及撤銷指示，電子版與紙本具同等法律效力。
body: 政府表示，香港市民最快明年可在醫健通平台以電子方式訂立預設醫療指示，列明一旦患上末期疾病時不希望接受哪些維持生命治療。
勞工及福利局局長孫玉菡周三在書面回覆立法會議員時表示，目前只以紙本形式存在的電子服務將分階段推出，經諮詢包括醫務衛生局在內的政府單位後，醫健通將作為指定電子系統，供市民訂立、儲存及撤銷指示。
當局指電子版將具有與紙本相同的法律效力。不作心肺復蘇術命令則繼續以紙本形式處理。《維持生命治療預作決定條例》已於今年7月31日生效，允許具精神行為能力的成年人在見證人（包括註冊醫生）面前以書面訂立指示。
